title: Inventions That Changed the World
summary: The wheel, fire, the printing press, electricity and the telephone, and why they mattered.

steps.title: The wheel
sentences: The wheel was invented more than five thousand years ago, first used by potters and then for carts.
It made it easier to carry heavy loads and travel far.
Today wheels are in cars, trains, machines and even clocks.

steps.title: Printing
sentences: Before printing, books were copied by hand, so they were costly and rare.
In the 1400s Johannes Gutenberg in Europe made printing with movable metal type practical.
Books became cheaper and ideas spread faster.

steps.title: Electricity and light
sentences: In the 1800s scientists such as Michael Faraday learned how to make electricity.
Inventors such as Thomas Edison and Joseph Swan helped make practical electric lights.
Light, factories, fans and phones all depend on electricity today.

steps.title: Talking across distance
sentences: Alexander Graham Bell was awarded a patent for the telephone in 1876.
Later came radio, television and mobile phones.
Now we can talk to a person anywhere in the world in a moment.

facts: Many inventions were built on earlier ideas by many people, not by one person alone.
Paper was invented in China around two thousand years ago.
India's Aryabhata and other scholars gave the world important ideas in maths and astronomy.

quiz.q: What did Gutenberg make practical in Europe?
quiz.why: Gutenberg's printing press used movable metal type.

quiz.q: Who received the telephone patent in 1876?
quiz.why: Bell was awarded the patent in 1876.

quiz.q: About how old is the wheel?
quiz.why: The wheel is over five thousand years old.

notes: Invention credits are simplified; many people contributed to each.
